title: Invisible Maps of Trade
thesis: A portolan chart did not merely picture Mediterranean trade: by reducing land to a named coast and sea to a routable field, it made a commercial network appear natural while concealing the jurisdictions, labour, coercion and negotiated privileges that kept that network moving.
whyThisSite: Terra Chartarum can read the chart beside the VMN authority tables, route paths and commodity vocabulary, letting the reader compare the elegant visual promise of frictionless movement with the dated political arrangements beneath every call.

claims.claim: Portolan charts encode coasts, place-names, compass networks and practical sailing relations rather than a continuous territorial surface.
Venice’s maritime dominion depended on differentiated jurisdictions and negotiation, not a single uniform colonial status.
Ships, convoy organisation and specialised construction made mapped connectivity operational.
The published VMN layer models seven authored route sequences, dated port-authority phases and a controlled commodity vocabulary.
Cartographic omission is an active selection that can naturalise the interests of the map’s makers and users.
